newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Russian foreign minister meets Arafat in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Russian foreign minister meets Arafat in Gaza.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov met Palestinian Yasser Arafat in self-ruled Gaza on Friday after assuring Israel that Syria does not seek war.

Arafat returned to Gaza, via Egypt, after visiting several European capitals this week to seek help and support in persuading Israel to carry out its long-delayed troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.

"I explained to (the Europeans) the situation concerning the peace process and the obstacles...which are preventing the implementation of the signed agreement," Arafat said, referring to a 1995 Hebron deal with Israel's previous government.
Asked before beginning talks with Primakov if the Russian foreign minister's visit would help the Middle East peace process, Arafat replied: "No doubt."
Primakov met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Friday and tried to calm war jitters in the Jewish state.
"While in Damascus, and I told the prime minister, I had no impression that the Syrians were preparing any strike against Israel," Primakov said on Friday.
Primakov arrived in Israel after holding talks with Syrian, Lebanese and Egyptian leaders.
In Jerusalem, U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk held an unscheduled meeting with Netanyahu after the cabinet's weekly session, which discussed Hebron.

The main U.S. mediator in four weeks of Israel-PLO talks on Hebron, Dennis Ross, returned home this week after the sides failed to strike a deal over terms for the redeployment from the town where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Arabs.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators continued talks while Ross and Arafat were away but Netanyahu, seeking tougher security measures to protect the settlers, charged the PLO leader was trying to delay a final agreement.

Israeli officials have speculated that Arafat aimed to postpone an accord until after Tuesday's U.S. presidential election in the hope that a second-term or new, incoming administration would pressure Israel into a pullback.
Arafat has denied the allegation. "We want an honest implementation of the (1995 Hebron) agreement," he said on Friday.
U.S. officials said they did not expect Ross to return to the region before the second half of next week.
Before returning to Gaza, Arafat briefed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on his trip to Europe and the latest developments in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations, official sources said in Cairo.
